title: used to, would and past habits
titleVi: used to, would và thói quen trong quá khứ
summary: Nói về thói quen và trạng thái đã chấm dứt, đồng thời phân biệt với be/get used to + V-ing.
whyItMatters: Trong Speaking Part 1 và 2, câu hỏi về tuổi thơ và thay đổi cuộc sống xuất hiện liên tục. `used to` là công cụ gọn nhất để nói 'trước đây thì...', nhưng chỉ cần nhầm với `be used to + V-ing` là câu mất điểm ngay. Đây cũng là cấu trúc ăn điểm khi so sánh quá khứ với hiện tại trong Task 2.

sections.heading: used to + infinitive: past states and finished habits
body: **used to + base verb** describes something that was true in the past but is not true now — either a repeated habit or a state.

It is the only structure that handles both habits (*I used to walk to school*) and states (*There used to be a market here*). The past simple handles habits but not states: *I walked to school* is fine, but *There was a market here* loses the contrast with now.
Because the meaning already contains 'past', you cannot say *I use to* in the present, and there is no present form of this structure.

examples.right: I used to walk to school every morning.
examples.note: A past habit that has stopped.

examples.right: There used to be a market on this corner.
examples.note: A past state — no present equivalent.

examples.right: She didn't use to enjoy reading, but now she reads daily.
examples.wrong: She didn't used to enjoy reading, but now she reads daily.

examples.right: Did you use to live in the countryside?

sections.heading: would: repeated actions, never states
body: **would + base verb** also describes repeated past actions, and it gives a nostalgic, storytelling tone: *Every summer we would visit my grandmother in Hue.*
The restriction is decisive: **would** cannot describe past states. Say *I used to have a motorbike*, never *I would have a motorbike*.
In exam writing, **would** is rare outside narrative; **used to** and the past simple with a frequency expression are safer choices.

examples.right: Every summer we would visit my grandmother in Hue.
examples.note: Repeated action with a nostalgic tone.

examples.right: My father used to own a small bookshop.
examples.wrong: My father would own a small bookshop.
examples.note: **own** is a state — only **used to** works.

examples.right: On rainy days, the children would play cards for hours.

sections.heading: Past simple with frequency expressions
body: The past simple plus a frequency expression can also express a past habit: *I played football every afternoon when I was a child.*
This is the least marked option and the safest in academic writing. Use **used to** when you want to stress the contrast with the present, and the past simple when the contrast is irrelevant.
With a definite time span, the past simple is often better: *Between 2005 and 2010, I studied in Da Nang* — not *I used to study*, because the period is bounded and complete.

examples.right: I played football every afternoon when I was a child.
examples.note: Past habit without emphasis on the contrast.

examples.right: Between 2005 and 2010, I studied in Da Nang.
I used to play football every afternoon, but now I have no time.
examples.note: **used to** highlights the contrast with now.

sections.heading: used to + V versus be/get used to + V-ing
body: These two structures look almost identical and mean completely different things. **used to + base verb** = a finished past habit. **be used to + -ing/noun** = be accustomed to something.
**get used to + -ing** describes the process of becoming accustomed: *It took me a year to get used to the cold.*
The test is grammatical: if a base verb follows, it is the past habit; if an -ing form or a noun follows, it is familiarity.

rows: past habit or state, now finished
I used to live in Hue.
I am used to living in a big city.
She got used to the night shift.

sections.heading: Comparing past and present in IELTS
body: Task 2 often contrasts generations: *Thirty years ago, most families used to eat at home, whereas today...* This gives your argument a temporal dimension without extra words.
In Task 1, **used to** is not appropriate for data. Charts report figures (*In 1990, the figure stood at 20%*), not habits. Reserve **used to** for people and general social behaviour.

In Speaking Part 2, combine **used to** for background with the past simple for the specific event: *We used to spend every summer at my aunt's farm, and one year I decided to stay for the whole harvest.*

examples.right: Thirty years ago, most families used to eat at home, whereas today many rely on delivery apps.
examples.note: Contrast between past and present in Task 2.

examples.wrong: In 1990, the figure used to stand at 20%.
examples.note: Số liệu biểu đồ không dùng **used to**.

examples.right: We used to spend every summer at my aunt's farm.

commonMistakes.wrong: I am used to walk to school when I was a child.
commonMistakes.right: I used to walk to school when I was a child.
commonMistakes.why: `be used to + V-ing` nghĩa là 'quen với', không phải 'đã từng'. Thói quen quá khứ đã chấm dứt dùng `used to + động từ nguyên mẫu`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I would have a dog when I was a child.
commonMistakes.right: I used to have a dog when I was a child.
commonMistakes.why: `Would` chỉ dùng cho hành động lặp lại, không dùng cho trạng thái. `Have a dog` là trạng thái nên phải dùng `used to`.

commonMistakes.wrong: I didn't used to like coffee.
commonMistakes.right: I didn't use to like coffee.
commonMistakes.why: Sau trợ động từ `didn't`, dùng `use to` không có `-d`. Đây là lỗi chính tả nhưng bị tính là lỗi ngữ pháp.

commonMistakes.wrong: I used to living in Da Nang.
commonMistakes.right: I used to live in Da Nang.
commonMistakes.why: `Used to` + động từ nguyên mẫu. Dạng `-ing` chỉ đúng khi đi với `be/get used to`.

commonMistakes.wrong: In 2010, the unemployment rate used to be 8%.
commonMistakes.why: Số liệu của một năm cụ thể không phải thói quen, nên không dùng `used to`. Đây là lỗi thường gặp khi mô tả biểu đồ Task 1.

ieltsTips: Dùng `used to` để tạo tương phản quá khứ - hiện tại trong Task 2: `Thirty years ago, families used to ..., whereas now ...`
Không dùng `used to` cho số liệu Task 1; biểu đồ mô tả con số tại một thời điểm, không mô tả thói quen.
Trong Speaking Part 2, một câu `used to` ở phần mở đầu giúp dựng bối cảnh nhanh, sau đó chuyển sang `past simple` cho sự kiện chính.
Kiểm tra nhanh: nếu sau cụm từ là động từ nguyên mẫu thì đó là thói quen quá khứ; nếu là `V-ing` hoặc danh từ thì đó là 'quen với'.

exercises.question: There ___ a cinema on this street, but it closed in 2005.
exercises.explanation: Trạng thái trong quá khứ, nay không còn → **used to be**. **Would** không dùng cho trạng thái.

exercises.question: Which sentence expresses a past habit correctly?
options: I am used to walk to school when I was a child.
I used to walk to school when I was a child.
I used to walking to school when I was a child.
I would walked to school when I was a child.
exercises.explanation: Thói quen quá khứ đã chấm dứt → **used to + động từ nguyên mẫu**.

exercises.question: After six months in Hanoi, she ___ the traffic.
exercises.explanation: Diễn tả trạng thái 'đã quen với' ở hiện tại → **be used to + noun**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is NOT correct?
options: My father used to own a small shop.
My father would own a small shop.
My father owned a small shop.
My father used to work in a small shop.
exercises.explanation: **own** là trạng thái nên không dùng **would** cho thói quen quá khứ.

exercises.question: We ___ (spend) every summer at my grandmother's house when I was young.
exercises.hint: thói quen quá khứ đã chấm dứt
exercises.explanation: Thói quen lặp lại trong quá khứ, nay không còn → **used to + V**.

exercises.question: It took me a year to ___ (get) the night shift.
exercises.explanation: Quá trình trở nên quen với việc gì → **get used to + noun**.

exercises.question: ___ play tennis before your injury? (câu hỏi với used to)
exercises.hint: Câu hỏi: did + you + use to + V
exercises.explanation: Câu hỏi dùng **did + you + use to + V**.

exercises.question: In 1990, the unemployment rate ___ (stand) at 8%.
exercises.hint: số liệu một năm cụ thể
exercises.explanation: Số liệu tại một thời điểm cụ thể dùng **past simple**, không dùng **used to**.

exercises.question: She ___ (not / use) like spicy food, but now she loves it.
exercises.explanation: Phủ định là **didn't use to + V** (không có **-d** ở **use**).
